stem.text: Let f and g be continuous functions with \( \int_{0}^{8} f(x)\,dx = -6 \), \( \int_{5}^{8} f(x)\,dx = 2 \), and \( \int_{5}^{0} g(x)\,dx = 2 \). Find the value of \( \int_{0}^{5} \left(4f(x) - 3g(x)\right) dx \).

worked_solution.text: Reverse the given integral of g: \( \int_{0}^{5} g(x)\,dx = -(2) = -2 \), and use linearity on the requested integral.

difficulty_variables.whether a reversal of limits is required: yes, one supplied integral runs right to left
difficulty_variables.whether a constant multiple or a sum app: a linear combination of two functions

distractor_derivations.A: given integral of g from 5 to 0 used as if it ran from 0 to 5
distractor_derivations.B: split written with its limits reversed, taking the integral of f from 0 to 5 as 2 - (-6)
distractor_derivations.D: integral of f from 8 to 5 taken as 2 instead of -2
